solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loans saved, can make a move

indicators.note: to make a move is to shift position, so the letters of these two words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Money put aside in a tin lets someone take action, as a lender might advise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a move' rearranges SAVED and CAN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums of money paid out ahead of time on credit are loans, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Swallow or dove circling over ancient city

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second
a bird circling wheels about, so the letters of the bird are turned into a new order

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city of Abraham, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a swallow or a dove wheeling above the ruins of an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird keeping company with the dove, but it is the verb meaning to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour food is to swallow it greedily, a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: A student's destiny to get grant

parts.note: L is the learner plate letter, standing for a student
one's lot in life is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A student's future depends on getting a funding grant.
explanation.walkthrough: The grant looks like student funding, but it is the verb meaning to assign.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a share to someone is to apportion it to them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Force prisoners to take exercise

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts
to train is to exercise or work out

explanation.surface: Inmates are compelled to do physical exercise in the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel someone by pressure is to force them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Pins inserted into joints

parts.note: joints suggest the body's knees and elbows, as in surgical pins, but these are joints of meat pierced by long metal spikes for roasting

explanation.surface: A surgeon fixes metal pins into a patient's damaged joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joints' points to anatomy; the joints here are cuts of meat on the spit.
explanation.definitionFit: Long metal or wooden spits pushed through meat to hold it while cooking are skewers.

clue.text: Where the Ark went fast

parts.note: fast suggests speed, but here it means stuck firm: Noah's vessel came to rest aground on this mountain

explanation.surface: A question about how quickly Noah's vessel sailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as speedy; in Genesis the Ark settled firmly on the mountains of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis says Noah's vessel came to rest on the mountains of Ararat when the flood waters fell.

clue.text: Unfortunately one is taken in by it

definitions.text: Unfortunately one is taken in by it

indicators.note: one item taken in by another is held inside it, so the numeral goes within the regretful exclamation

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning sadly or unfortunately
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that people are, sadly, deceived by something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a false name is something people are taken in by.
explanation.definitionFit: An assumed name used to deceive is the thing people get taken in by.

clue.text: Appearing every second

parts.note: every second suggests each tick of the clock, but it means every other one in a sequence

explanation.surface: Something that shows up constantly, once each second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every second' reads as a unit of time, but it means every other one.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring on every other day or in every other position is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Particularly the highest

definitions.meaning: especially or more than anything else
read literally, higher than everything else, at the very top

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means especially, and taken word by word it describes what sits over everything else.

clue.text: Name for girls and boys, evenly distributed

indicators.note: letters distributed are spread out and set down in a new order

explanation.surface: A name given equally often to daughters and sons, shared out fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges EVENLY.
explanation.definitionFit: This name has been borne by men, such as the writer Waugh, as well as by women.

clue.text: A compulsory turn-out

parts.note: turn-out suggests attendance at an event that everyone must join, but here people are turned out of their home

explanation.surface: An event that everyone is required to attend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-out' looks like an attendance figure, but it means being turned out of a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally removing tenants from a property forces them out whether they like it or not.

clue.text: Blue tits flying offer something deaf people may appreciate

indicators.note: birds flying flit about, so the letters of these two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Birds on the wing present something that hard-of-hearing people would enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges BLUE TITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Captions printed under film dialogue let people who cannot hear follow the speech.

clue.text: Cycle chain?

definitions.meaning: a cycle of plays or poems is a connected sequence
a chain of events is a succession of linked items

explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a connected sequence of things following one another.

clue.text: Change sides

parts.note: suggests switching allegiance, but change is loose coins and these are the two faces of a coin

explanation.surface: An instruction to defect to the opposing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like a verb; it is loose coins, whose two faces are called for in a toss.
explanation.definitionFit: The two faces of a coin are what a person calls when it is tossed.

clue.text: An all-star cast?

parts.note: suggests a film full of celebrities, but the stars are planets and constellations and cast means calculated

explanation.surface: A film boasting a line-up of famous actors.
explanation.walkthrough: An astrologer casts this chart from the positions of the stars, so 'cast' and 'star' both shift sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrological chart is cast, drawn up, from the positions of the stars and planets.

clue.text: Possibly terrorise a noisy carouser

indicators.note: signals that the letters might possibly be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A rowdy reveller might well frighten people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TERRORISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A boisterous reveller who parties loudly is a synonym for a noisy carouser.

clue.text: Work shop?

definitions.meaning: one's line of trade or occupation
a firm or commercial concern, such as a shop

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one's occupation and a commercial enterprise such as a store.

clue.text: Today's charge for electricity?

parts.note: read as the present cost, but current is also electric flow, so this is the price of the flow

explanation.surface: A query about the latest energy tariff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Today's charge' means the present price; current is electricity, giving a second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The present market cost of something; current also names flowing electricity.

clue.text: Formed a queue at the back

definitions.text: Formed a queue at the back

parts.words: Formed a queue at the back
parts.note: suggests joining the end of a line of people, but a queue is also a pigtail worn at the back of the head

explanation.surface: Someone joined the line at its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queue' is the old word for a pigtail, braided at the back of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair braided into a pigtail has been woven in strands, as the past participle says.

clue.text: Irishman goes to church for spiritual guidance

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irishman attends church seeking guidance for his soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiritual' suggests religion, but this is a meeting to contact spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting in which people seek messages from the spirits of the dead is a loose sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Did not see but heard spray

indicators.note: something heard is spoken, so the word for spray is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: mist is a fine spray of droplets

explanation.surface: Someone failed to spot something but could hear water spraying.
explanation.definitionFit: If you failed to notice something, you overlooked it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stay and brood

definitions.meaning: to remain or live in a place
to ... on something is to brood over it

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to reside somewhere and to linger on a troubling thought.

clue.text: Legal man shifting on treaty

indicators.note: letters shifting move around into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawyer changes his position regarding an international agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges ON and TREATY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer authorised to act for others is a legal professional, a synonym.

clue.text: Hood and sash worn in Royal Navy

indicators.note: the garment worn in the navy is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: an obi is the broad sash worn with a Japanese kimono

explanation.surface: A hood and a sash form part of a naval uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' looks like headwear; it is Robin Hood, the outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest is known by this first name and surname Hood.

clue.text: Suggestive of financial aid in hiring charge

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: rent is what is charged for hiring property
the dole is state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A hint that state support is being swallowed up by rental costs.
explanation.walkthrough: THE DOLE is the British name for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that evokes or calls to mind another thing is reminiscent or suggestive of it.

clue.text: Manages to rope in live artist

indicators.note: roping something in draws it inside, so the verb for exist is enclosed

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone in charge recruits a painter who is still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' looks like an adjective describing the artist, but it is the verb, giving BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was a celebrated Flemish Baroque painter.

clue.text: Also seen in the guise of a dandy

parts.note: a swell is a fashionably dressed man, a dandy

explanation.surface: Someone else is also spotted, dressed up as a fashionable gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in the guise of' is a link: the answer is A SWELL, a dandy, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition or too, a synonym of the adverb.

clue.text: Not all there being called into action

indicators.note: one piece put into another goes inside it

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: A person summoned into service is not entirely present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mad or mentally unbalanced is informally said to be not all there.
